title: Video-Language Models: Temporal Tokens and Grounding

questions.question: What is the first timestamp returned by uniform_sample(duration=10.0, n=8)?
options: 1.25 seconds, because each sample spans two bins
0.0 seconds, because sampling begins at the left boundary
0.625 seconds, the midpoint of the first 10/8-second bin
10.0 seconds, because duration is repeated for every frame
questions.explanation: The function uses step=duration/n=1.25 and samples at step*(i+0.5). For i=0 the first timestamp is 0.625 seconds.

questions.question: How does dynamic_sample allocate frames when the per-second motion values are uneven?
options: It gives every second exactly one frame and ignores motion
It samples only the first second with nonzero motion
It sorts the video seconds and changes their chronological order
It gives more samples to high-motion seconds, while respecting fps_cap and a minimum of one
questions.explanation: Each second receives a motion-proportional rounded count, clipped to at most fps_cap and at least one. The generated timestamps remain within their original seconds.

questions.question: What IoU does the jump prediction [4.1,4.7] have against ground truth [4.0,4.5]?
options: About 0.57, because the intersection is 0.4 and the union is 0.7
0.30, exactly the evaluator threshold
0.40, using only the intersection duration
1.00, because the event names match
questions.explanation: The interval intersection is [4.1,4.5] with length 0.4. The union spans [4.0,4.7] with length 0.7, so iou returns 0.4/0.7 ≈ 0.571.

questions.question: What recall does evaluate_grounding report for the three demo events at tol_iou=0.3?
options: 1.00, because jump, turn, and sit each exceed IoU 0.3
0.33, because only jump clears the IoU threshold
0.67, because sit falls below the threshold
0.00, because predictions must have identical boundaries
questions.explanation: The demo produces IoUs of about 0.57 for jump, 0.29 for turn, and 0.27 for sit. Only jump clears 0.3, so hits/len(ground_truth) is 1/3 ≈ 0.33.

questions.question: Which architecture row pairs Qwen2.5-VL with its temporal design?
options: Q-former per clip and a fixed audio branch
MLP over eight frames with no temporal positions
TMRoPE with dynamic FPS and absolute time
A pooled image-only encoder with no video support
questions.explanation: arch_compare labels Qwen2.5-VL as TMRoPE / dynamic FPS and notes absolute time. That distinguishes it from fixed-clip Q-Former designs.

questions.question: What is the central difference between Video-LLaMA and Video-LLaVA in arch_compare?
options: Video-LLaMA is text-only and Video-LLaVA is an audio codec
Both use exactly the same compressor and only differ in benchmark names
Video-LLaMA uses TMRoPE and Video-LLaVA uses no visual encoder
Video-LLaMA uses Q-former per clip with an audio branch, while Video-LLaVA uses an MLP over frames
questions.explanation: The table lists Video-LLaMA as Q-former / 16 frames with a fixed clip and audio branch, and Video-LLaVA as MLP / 8 frames with a shared image-video encoder.
